best_for: Employees and admins whose company runs OpenVPN Access Server or CloudConnexa and who were handed a profile file or server address to connect with.
description:
OpenVPN Connect is the desktop app from OpenVPN Inc. for joining a virtual private network that runs on the OpenVPN protocol. It is proprietary software, and on Windows you can also get it from the Microsoft Store or through winget.

Once a profile is loaded, you connect with a single toggle, and a status indicator tells you when the tunnel is up. You can send the connection through a proxy, add certificates and tokens, and sign in with a plain password, SAML single sign-on or multi-factor authentication, whichever your server asks for. The Windows app also has command-line controls, so IT can script its setup.

points.title: A client, not a VPN service
points.text: OpenVPN Connect does not come with servers. You need a connection profile, either an .ovpn file or a server URL, from your IT team or a VPN provider. Without one, there is nothing to connect to.

points.title: The servers are where the cost is
points.text: The app is free to download. The paid part is the server side: Access Server's free tier allows only two connections at once, and a third device is refused until one disconnects.

points.title: Works with OpenVPN's own servers
points.text: Profiles import by URL from Access Server or with a CloudConnexa ID, and other OpenVPN-compatible services can be imported as a profile file.

points.title: Sign in to Windows over the VPN
points.text: Version 3.9.0 for Windows can connect before you log in, so a remote laptop can reach the domain at the sign-in screen. An admin has to set it up, and it does not support device posture checks or ePKI certificates.

points.title: Mac users must approve an extension
points.text: From 3.9.0 the Mac app uses Apple's Network Extension framework. After upgrading you have to approve the OpenVPN extension when macOS asks, or connections fail.

points.title: Older systems are out
points.text: The Windows app no longer installs on Windows 7 or 8. The Mac installers listed here have separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds and need macOS 12 or later.

points.title: No Linux build here
points.text: This site lists Windows and macOS only. The Windows installers are 32-bit and 64-bit MSI packages that install for all users, which suits company rollouts. The Windows listing keeps 20 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
